chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Abu Hafth al-Jurjani from Abu al-Khadib al-Rabi' ibn Bakr from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever trims his fingernails and mustache every Friday and says when he does so: 'In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)', not a clipping of his nails nor a hair of his mustache will fall without Allah recording for him the freeing of a soul, and he will not fall ill except with the illness in which he dies."

key_terms.سُنَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for trimming nails and mustache on Friday in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) is considered a weekly Eid, and this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the ritual purity (taharah) associated with it by linking grooming to spiritual liberation. The promise that no nail or hair falls without recording the emancipation of a slave underscores the cumulative value of small, consistent acts of worship. Furthermore, the guarantee of health until death reflects the holistic view of physical well-being as a component of divine favor for the faithful.
